title: FieldOps — See the signal. Act in time.
revision: Stable framing, complete panels, verified evidence

segments.text: Growers check traps by hand. Between visits, pests keep moving—and treatment windows can close.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: FieldOps connects trap photos, pest activity, and weather to answer two questions: which block needs attention, and when? Our drone concept adds farm-wide visual context.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Now explore the working dashboard. Six blocks. Eighteen traps. One connected orchard. Rotate the three-dimensional farm, follow the simulated survey, and open each capture without losing the bigger picture.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Go closer. Inspect labeled reference images, separate from the season’s trap records. Compare species counts, explore the sample annotations, and review daily observations, block by block.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Watch the season unfold. Flight curves reveal sustained pest activity. Compare pressure across blocks. Sustained catch starts the clock. Temperature advances it, turning daily observations into a clear timeline.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Here is the moment that matters. June fourth. Block C. Twenty-six codling moths and two hundred sixty-one degree-days since biofix. The treatment window is open—and the dashboard makes it impossible to miss.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Want the reason? Ask FieldOps. The assistant explains the selected facts, with a natural voice generated right on the GB10.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Block C: Spray window open. The authoritative timeline records biofix on May 8. Block C has 261.0 degree-days since that recorded start.
segments.speaker: FieldOps / GB10

segments.text: And the grower does not have to sit at a dashboard. Here is the real Telegram workflow: send a trap photo, get the marked-up image, species counts, and block context back on the phone.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Behind it all: local vision, deterministic timing, and an agent workflow built with NemoClaw, OpenClaw, and OpenShell. Inference stays on the Dell GB10. Telegram carries the message. The decision comes from the evidence.
segments.speaker: narrator

segments.text: Less manual counting. Earlier visibility. One clear next action. FieldOps helps growers focus attention where—and when—it matters.
segments.speaker: narrator
